data.name: Dhurv
data.gender_notes: Dhurv is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Dhurv is a Sanskrit name derived from the word 'dhruva', which means 'fixed' or 'stable'. In Hindu mythology, Dhurv is the name of a celestial mountain and the pole star around which the heavens revolve. As such, Dhurv represents the unchanging and stable aspect of the universe. The name Dhurv carries the meaning “Ruler of the Cosmos” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Dhurv usually hope their child will grow to embody ruler of the cosmos and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of unwavering faith and inner calm.

It represents stability and constancy, much like how these celestial bodies are regarded as unchanging entities in the universe. The belief in the power of names and their divine origins has been an integral part of Hindu culture, which is reflected in the reverence given to this name.

historical_references.reference: In ancient Hindu texts, Dhurv is mentioned as a sage who is one of the seven great sages (Saptarshis) in the constellation of Ursa Major. The Saptarshis were believed to guide the planets in their celestial orbits.

Dhurv is also known as the patron god of the Vedic deity Indra, who is the god of rains, storms, and war. According to Hindu mythology, Dhurv was a powerful sage who performed a severe penance to please Indra, who was then blessed with the power to destroy the demons that threatened the universe.
